main_text.l: ti, iamdudum ante ipse, eruditissime Leo,
inculcasti ex Græcorum, & Latinorum
consensu, quod plurimum Reformatorum
latera vrget, & pectora ferit. Videns dein
Bartholdus Nihusius ذو الذكر الـمـالـك [?]
quisque pro bono Ecclesiæ longiori vita di-
gnus erat, idem hoc argumentum maiores
sumere vires ex aliorum Orientalium con-
sensione, duo nostro Hebediesu, dum illum
vna cum nostris notis recudi curauit Mo-
guntiæ, adiecit programmata ad Acade-
micos Protestantes, quibus eos prouocat ad
singulare hoc certamen. Præsertim cum non
defuerint apud ipsos, qui meris, & nudis as-
sertionibus Orientalium hunc consensum
sibi vindicare sint conati, vti testis vberri-
mus, & omni exceptione maior, nobis esse
potest vir clarissimus Iulius Blumius, qui
vna nobiscum plures huius generis assertio-
nes contulit Parisijs. Huius autem argu-
menti ex consensione tot populorum ad-
structum, vim, & efficaciam effugere, atq;
euitare volentes Veielius, & Hottingerus,
opposita prorsus diuerticula, & flexiones
arripiunt, eodem tamen collimantes, neminem
veritatem ipsam eludere. Veielius enim,
vt se hinc citius expediat, hunc irridet, &
improbat consensum, ita pag. 2. scribens:

page.notes: The Arabic line between "Videns dein" and "quisque" is marked [?] because the letters are not fully legible at this scan resolution. The line may be a set-off author name with an Arabic phrase, and the Arabic is uncertain. "opposita" has a Cyrillic-looking "a" in the printed text; it is a Latin word, so the letters should be Latin, and it is written here as printed with the doubtful letter flagged for review. The left edge of the scan shows the neighbouring page and is not transcribed.
